titleBn: সেফটি কোড (Safety Code): সুরক্ষার স্থানীয় আইন
liveLevelTitleBn: সেফটি কোড (Safety Code): সুরক্ষার স্থানীয় আইন

board.mythBn: এত বছর ধরে কাজ করছি, আমার পারমিট বা আর্থিং লাগে না, আমি হাত দিয়েই ভোল্টেজ বুঝি।

rounds.promptBn: পোলে ওঠার আগে আপনার হাতে কোন কাগজ থাকবে?
safe: Written PTW slip whose book number and time match the permit-book page beside it
Lineman reading the permit page (feeder, time, job) before signing, pen still capped

traps.what: Lineman on the phone at the pole foot, 'line off' by voice, no paper
traps.rejectBn: ফোনে মুখের কথায় লাইন অফ আছে বিশ্বাস করবেন না—লিখিত পারমিট চাই।

traps.what: Signing the permit book without reading, eyes on the pole
traps.rejectBn: সই করার আগে পড়ে নিন কোন ফিডার, কোন সময় আর কী কাজের জন্য পারমিট।

traps.what: Climbing an 11 kV pole with no permit at all
traps.rejectBn: পারমিট ছাড়া উঠে দুর্ঘটনা ঘটলে কোম্পানি কোনো দায়িত্ব নেয় না; CEI তদন্তে জেল পর্যন্ত হতে পারে।

traps.what: Permit slip whose number and time do not match the book
traps.rejectBn: পারমিট বইয়ের নম্বর এবং সময় মিলিয়ে দেখুন—না মিললে কাজ নয়।

rounds.promptBn: ব্রেকার অফ করার পর কোনটা আইন মানছে?
safe: Breaker at OFF with the lineman's padlock through it and a 'কাজ চলছে' board
Lineman putting the padlock key into his own shirt pocket

traps.what: Breaker at OFF, no lock, no board
traps.rejectBn: ভুল করে কেউ যেন ব্রেকার অন না করে দেয়—হ্যান্ডেলে তালা আর 'কাজ চলছে' বোর্ড চাই।

traps.what: Padlock on, key left in the lock
traps.rejectBn: চাবিটা নিজের পকেটে রাখুন—আপনার জীবন আপনার পকেটে।

traps.what: Lineman handing his key to another person at the panel
traps.rejectBn: নিজের তালা, নিজের চাবি—চাবি অন্যের হাতে মানে জীবন অন্যের হাতে।

traps.what: Only a 'কাজ চলছে' board hung, no padlock
traps.rejectBn: বোর্ড একা যথেষ্ট নয়—ব্রেকার অফ করে হ্যান্ডেলে তালাও লাগাতে হবে।

rounds.promptBn: রাস্তার ওপর 11 kV লাইন—কোন ছবিটা আইন মানছে?
safe: 11 kV span high over the road, a loaded truck far below the lowest point
Lineman on patrol looking along the span, logbook in hand

traps.what: 11 kV span sagging low, truck top close under it
traps.rejectBn: 11 kV লাইন মাটি থেকে অন্তত 18–19 ফুট উঁচুতে থাকতে হবে।

traps.what: Covered 11 kV conductor sagging low, people reaching from a truck
traps.rejectBn: কভার্ড কন্ডাক্টরকেও বেয়ার ধরার আইন—পিন-হোল বা ফাটল থাকতে পারে।

traps.what: Lineman walking past an obviously sagging span without writing
traps.rejectBn: লাইন ঝুলে গেলে তা টাইট করা আপনার আইনি দায়িত্ব।

rounds.promptBn: বাড়ির পাশ দিয়ে LT লাইন—কোনটা ঠিক দূরত্বে?
safe: LT line well clear of a balcony where a woman dries clothes
LT line beside a terrace with a wide horizontal gap, a child at the rail

traps.what: LT wire within arm's reach of a balcony rail
traps.rejectBn: LT লাইন বাড়ি বা বারান্দা থেকে অনুভূমিক 1.2 মিটার দূরে থাকার কথা।

traps.what: Clothes line from the balcony almost touching the LT wire
traps.rejectBn: কাপড় মেলতে গিয়ে কেউ যেন তারে না লাগে—সেজন্যই বিল্ডিং ক্লিয়ারেন্স।

traps.what: Man leaning out of a window, hand toward the LT wire
traps.rejectBn: কেউ যেন হাত বাড়িয়ে তারে না লাগে—তার বাড়ি থেকে আইনের দূরত্বে চাই।

rounds.promptBn: বন্ধ লাইনে কাজ—অস্থায়ী আর্থিং কোনটা ঠিক?
safe: Earth rod on the line at the pole before and the pole after the work pole, brass chain over the phases at both
Lineman holding the discharge rod to the line first, chain still coiled on his shoulder

traps.what: Earth set on only one side of the work pole
traps.rejectBn: কাজের জায়গার আগে ও পরে—দুই প্রান্তে অস্থায়ী আর্থিং বাধ্যতামূলক।

traps.what: Ball-chain thrown over the line, no rod anywhere
traps.rejectBn: চেইন শুধু ফেজ শর্ট করে; রড চার্জ নামায়—শর্ট সার্কিট ≠ আর্থিং।

traps.what: A rusty grey iron jugaad chain with a broken link on the line
traps.rejectBn: মরিচা, ভাঙা বা লোহার জুগাড় চেইন বারণ—সন্দেহ হলে পোলে ওঠার আগেই বদলান।

traps.what: Bare hand on a 'dead' line with no earth on it
traps.rejectBn: Dead লাইনকেও Live মনে করতে হবে যতক্ষণ না সেটা আর্থ করা হচ্ছে।

rounds.promptBn: অভিজ্ঞতা নয়, আইন—কোন হাত কাজের জন্য তৈরি?
safe: Whole rubber gloves and whole boots on a lineman at the van
Lineman taking his own discharge rod and chain in hand before climbing

traps.what: Torn glove fingertip reaching for a tool
traps.rejectBn: ছেঁড়া গ্লাভস পরে কাজ আর খালি হাতে কাজ একই ব্যাপার—দুটোই বেআইনি এবং বিপজ্জনক।

traps.what: Boot with a torn sole, toes showing
traps.rejectBn: ছেঁড়া জুতো পরে কাজ করাও খালি হাতে কাজের মতোই বেআইনি আর বিপজ্জনক।

traps.what: Grey-haired lineman touching a conductor with the back of his hand
traps.rejectBn: বিদ্যুৎ কাউকে চেনে না—অতি-আত্মবিশ্বাসী অভিজ্ঞরাই বেশি দুর্ঘটনার শিকার।

traps.what: Lineman about to climb trusting a mate's word that the earth is on
traps.rejectBn: পোলে ওঠার আগে নিজের হাতে রড ও চেইন নিন; অন্যকে বিশ্বাস করবেন না।

deadlySlipTable.act: Climbing / starting work on a phone or verbal 'line off' without the written PTW in hand (incl. listening to the coworker who pushes it)
deadlySlipTable.source: 8.10 pro tip 1; 8.5 PTW; Module 1 step 17 owner ruling. Used: do_8_10_a, gate
deadlySlipTable.rulingNote: Confirmed (M1 step 17 / B7). Live 8.10 pro tip 1 now reads written permit AND own earthing (see N1/M8-17 for the tester).

deadlySlipTable.act: Climbing / pressing 'উঠি' without rod earth on both sides of the work span
deadlySlipTable.source: 8.5 two-end temporary earthing; Module 1 step 15; Module 4 4.1a/4.7b. Used: do_8_5_b, gate
deadlySlipTable.rulingNote: Confirmed (M1 step 15; WBSEDCL SM earths both sides; live 8.5).

deadlySlipTable.act: Throwing the shorting chain as the earth before that end's rod has drained and earthed the line (incl. listening to myth 3)
deadlySlipTable.source: 8.5 myth 3 reality; Module 1 step 15 'chain instead of rod'. Used: do_8_5_b

deadlySlipTable.act: Passing a too-low 11 kV span or a too-close LT span on ground patrol
deadlySlipTable.source: 8.5 clearances (harm to the public; patrol on the ground)
deadlySlipTable.rulingNote: DRAFT: slip (ground patrol, M5-3). Road height per live 8.5 and A2: 11 kV 6.5 m (not 18-19 ft).

deadlySlipTable.act: Padlock key not in own pocket (left on the hook board or handed to the operator)
deadlySlipTable.source: 8.5 pro tip 2 'আপনার জীবন আপনার পকেটে'; both earth ends still protect the climber
deadlySlipTable.rulingNote: DRAFT: slip (both rod earths still protect; M1 step 18).

deadlySlipTable.act: No padlock or no 'কাজ চলছে' board on the OFF handle
deadlySlipTable.source: 8.5 LOTO; Module 1 step 18 does not make LOTO deadly
deadlySlipTable.rulingNote: DRAFT: slip (M1 step 18 does not make LOTO deadly).

deadlySlipTable.act: Throwing a rusty / broken-link / bent-hook / iron jugaad chain after the rod has earthed that end
deadlySlipTable.source: 8.5 chain বারণীয় ('আইনি দায় + জীবনের ঝুঁকি'); contrast Module 1 step 14 jugaad ROD = deadly
deadlySlipTable.rulingNote: DRAFT: slip after the rod has earthed that end (the rod is the earth; M1 step 14 jugaad ROD stays deadly).

addedRows.act: Climbing, or a hand or tool on the line, after the shutdown but before the tester shows 0 V (incl. a skipped tester)
addedRows.howUsed: Scored in do_8_5_b (tester at the first end) and the gate (11th token টেস্টার). Shown done by the crew, without new scoring, in do_8_8_a (climb coda) and do_8_10_a (time-lapse).

changesGeneral: Unified rule: a wrong card in a 'why' reason deck costs the ◆ only; a wrong card in a field decision deck (what you say or do) costs a slip — applied across all levels and the gate.

Unified rule: the deadly class always sits on the CLIMB (permit, earth both ends, solar fuses) or the rod/chain order, never on hook removal, disconnection or paperwork; 8.2's disconnections and hook removal are abstract holds from the ground.

Bad (rusty/jugaad) chain thrown after the rod = slip, while Module 1 step 14 made a jugaad ROD deadly. Confirm the split.

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: Confirm the module rule: Module 8 deadly only for climb/earthing acts (written PTW, rod earth both ends, solar fuses out, rod-before-chain, clamp-before-hook) plus the gate's pre-shutdown trim; everything regulatory, billing, grievance, grid, environmental and ethical is a slip.
ownerDecisions.question: Module 8 is mostly law, bills and paperwork. Keep 'deadly' (level ends at once) only for climbing and earthing mistakes: no written permit, no rod earth at both ends, a solar fuse left in, chain before rod, rod hook before its clamp - plus cutting a branch on a live line in the gate? Everything about bills, notices, complaints, grid, environment and ethics = slip.
ownerDecisions.status: PENDING owner (sheet docs/review/m8_questions_2026-11-16.xlsx); DRAFT ruling M8-1 assumes the recommendation
ownerDecisions.options:
(a) Confirm, with the earlier deadly rows added.
(b) Add more deadly acts (say which).
ownerDecisions.recommended: (a) Every row matches an earlier ruling; nobody is near a live wire in the paperwork levels.
ownerDecisions.whatWeWillDo: Keep that list. Add the deadly rows earlier modules already made binding: climbing or touching before the tester shows 0 V, an earth put on a live line, and the Module 7 hook rules. Listening to the coworker takes the class of the act he pushes.
ownerDecisions.earlierRulings: M5-6 and M7-6 (nobody exposed = slip). M1 step 17 / B7 (no PTW = deadly). M1 step 15 (rod earth). M6-4 (rod hook before clamp = deadly). X1 / M5-2 (climb before 0 V = deadly). B8 (earth on a live line = deadly). M7-8 (hook). B1 (listening).

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: New deadly row: climbing with any solar fuse in (8.8a, gate) — deadly every time. Yes?
ownerDecisions.question: Lesson 8.8: a solar house can push power back into a 'dead' line. If the player climbs while any solar house's fuse is still in at the pole, is that deadly every time (even if that inverter would have switched off)?
ownerDecisions.status: PENDING owner (sheet docs/review/m8_questions_2026-11-16.xlsx); DRAFT ruling M8-2 assumes the recommendation
ownerDecisions.options:
(a) Deadly every time.
(b) Deadly only when the dealt inverter is faulty.
ownerDecisions.recommended: (a) The lineman cannot see whether the inverter works; the lesson says pull the fuse anyway.
ownerDecisions.whatWeWillDo: Deadly every time, in 8.8a and the gate. Listening to the coworker ('the inverter switches itself off') is deadly too. Pulling a non-solar house's fuse = slip.
ownerDecisions.earlierRulings: M1 step 15 (missing earth = deadly whether or not charge was there). B1 (listening). Lesson 8.8 pro tip 1 and the anti-islanding item ('ব্যাক-ফিড কারেন্টে মারা যাবে').

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: Gate C2: a pre-shutdown trim is deadly (4.8/do/0 precedent) — confirm, or drop C2 from the gate.
ownerDecisions.question: Gate: a branch rests on the LT line. If the player cuts it before the shutdown and permit, is that deadly? (Or drop this branch from the gate.)
ownerDecisions.status: PENDING owner (sheet docs/review/m8_questions_2026-11-16.xlsx); DRAFT ruling M8-3 assumes the recommendation
ownerDecisions.options:
(a) Deadly; keep it in the gate.
(b) Drop the branch from the gate.
ownerDecisions.recommended: (a) Cutting it puts the pruner on a live wire; same as Module 4.
ownerDecisions.whatWeWillDo: Deadly. After the permit it is the right act; cutting a harmless branch or the trunk = slip.
ownerDecisions.earlierRulings: Lesson 8.9 ('শাটডাউন নিয়ে ডাল কাটার সময়'). Module 4 tree level 4.8 precedent. B8 (a tool on a live line = deadly).

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: Frequency through 49.0 stays a slip (alternative: module-wide 'ব্ল্যাকআউট' deadly).
ownerDecisions.question: 8.4a (grid control room): if the frequency falls below 49.0 Hz before the player switches off the ordered feeders, is that a slip, or a deadly 'blackout'?
ownerDecisions.status: PENDING owner (sheet docs/review/m8_questions_2026-11-16.xlsx); DRAFT ruling M8-4 assumes the recommendation
ownerDecisions.options:
(a) Slip.
(b) Deadly 'ব্ল্যাকআউট' (then for the whole module).
ownerDecisions.recommended: (a) Nobody touches a live part; deadly stays for acts that can kill a person.
ownerDecisions.whatWeWillDo: Slip. The round still ends with the feeders off.
ownerDecisions.earlierRulings: M5-6 and M6-4 (harm to the system or equipment with nobody exposed = slip).

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: 8.5b splits: key not in own pocket, missing lock/board, bad chain after the rod, partial/skipped chain, early chain removal — all slips (Module 1 step 14 made a jugaad rod deadly). Confirm each.
ownerDecisions.question: 8.5b (earthing with rod and chain): are these all slips? Padlock key not in your own pocket; no padlock or no 'কাজ চলছে' board; a rusty or jugaad chain thrown after the rod has earthed; chain on only 1-2 phases or skipped; chains pulled down before clearance.
ownerDecisions.status: PENDING owner (sheet docs/review/m8_questions_2026-11-16.xlsx); DRAFT ruling M8-5 assumes the recommendation
ownerDecisions.options:
(a) All slips.
(b) Make some deadly (say which, e.g. the key).
ownerDecisions.recommended: (a) Same split as Module 1: the rod is the earth, the chain is extra.
ownerDecisions.whatWeWillDo: All slips. The rod earth at both ends is the protection and stays on. Chain before the rod, climbing without rod earth at both ends, and rod hook before its clamp stay deadly.
ownerDecisions.earlierRulings: M1 step 18 (LOTO faults not deadly). M1 step 14 (a jugaad ROD = deadly; the chain is not the earth). M6-4 (hook before clamp = deadly).

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: PCB oil without গ্লাভস/mask = slip; taking a bribe = slip. Confirm.
ownerDecisions.question: Two acts with slow or legal harm: handling old transformer oil (may hold PCBs) without গ্লাভস and mask, and taking cash to help with hooking. Both slips?
ownerDecisions.status: PENDING owner (sheet docs/review/m8_questions_2026-11-16.xlsx); DRAFT ruling M8-6 assumes the recommendation
ownerDecisions.options:
(a) Both slips.
(b) Make one deadly (say which).
ownerDecisions.recommended: (a) No shock or fall risk; the harm is slow or legal.
ownerDecisions.whatWeWillDo: Both slips. The PCB card says the oil can cause cancer and mask + গ্লাভস are compulsory; the bribe card says the law will not spare you.
ownerDecisions.earlierRulings: M5-6 (no shock or fall risk = slip). B6 (bad electrical gloves = deadly) is about shock, not oil.

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: Earth rod before the permit in the gate = slip (not in the lesson).
ownerDecisions.question: Gate: the player puts an earth rod on the line before the written permit. The design says slip. But before the permit the transformer is still ON, so the rod goes onto a live line. Deadly or slip?
ownerDecisions.status: PENDING owner (sheet docs/review/m8_questions_2026-11-16.xlsx); DRAFT ruling M8-7 assumes the recommendation
ownerDecisions.options:
(a) Deadly before the permit; slip after the permit but before the tester.
(b) Slip, as designed.
ownerDecisions.recommended: (a) B8 already makes an earth on a live line deadly everywhere.
ownerDecisions.whatWeWillDo: Deadly before the permit (earth on a live line). After the permit but before the tester shows 0 V = slip.
ownerDecisions.earlierRulings: B8 (earth on a live line = deadly in every module). X1 / M5-2 (earth before the tester = slip).

ownerDecisions.specQuestion: Reason-deck vs decision-deck rule (◆ only vs slip) for the whole module.
ownerDecisions.question: Wrong 'why' reason card = lose the ◆ only. Wrong card in a decision deck (what you say or do) = slip. Use this in the whole module?
ownerDecisions.status: PENDING owner (sheet docs/review/m8_questions_2026-11-16.xlsx); DRAFT ruling M8-8 assumes the recommendation
ownerDecisions.options:
(a) Yes.
(b) Other.
ownerDecisions.recommended: (a) Already the playbook rule.
ownerDecisions.whatWeWillDo: Yes, as in every module so far.
